summary: Teams & Collaboration backend tests: 25/25 passed. Covered auto-creation of personal workspace on register/login (idempotent), team CRUD (create/list/get/rename/delete), permission enforcement, invite flows (existing user immediate + pending-email auto-activation on register), member role management (promote, cannot change/remove owner), project team_id scoping, member access to shared projects (upload + annotate), non-member 403, team delete cascade (projects/images/versions/models), and demo user legacy compatibility (team_id migration).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~890 lines; consider splitting into modules (auth, teams, projects, images, training) for maintainability.
list_projects extends with legacy no-team_id projects but _ensure_personal_team migrates them on login/register - legacy branch is effectively dead once migrations run; can be removed.
DELETE /teams/{tid} uses `to_list(500)` for projects - could miss projects if a team has >500. Prefer async iteration or paginated delete.
invite_member returns 400 'User already a member' but does not distinguish active vs pending status; UX-wise consider returning 409 for conflict.
PATCH /teams/{tid}/members/{mid} does not validate that mid belongs to an active membership; role can be changed on a pending invite. Minor.
No index hints declared on team_members (team_id, user_id, status) - performance concern at scale.
test_credentials: demo@vf.io / demo1234 (existing). Test users created dynamically per run with test_a_*/test_b_*/test_pending_*/test_out_* email prefixes and password 'pass1234'.
seed_data_creation: Multiple TEST_ prefixed teams and projects were created during the run; some are left in DB (non-cascaded ones) — cleanup not implemented since tests use unique UUIDs each run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Teams backend fully validated by /app/tests/teams_smoke.py (25 tests, 100% pass). All team flows including invite auto-activation and cascade delete work. Use `_register()` helper which handles existing-user 400 by falling back to login. Auth token key is 'token' (not access_token). Fresh users per run avoid state pollution.
